findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget discards all actual table data
findings.body: When the organization has 'use-table-widget-visualization', tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns=[] and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}} instead of converting result.data/result.meta/fields from the query result. Because an empty array is not nullish, TableWidgetVisualization also does not derive columns from meta. Any dashboard table widget for such an org therefore renders an empty table and loses its data, title handling, custom field renderers, field aliases, and loading behavior.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only hidden while searching
findings.body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES ('is_segment', 'project_id', 'received') is only applied in the branch that runs when searchQuery is non-empty; when the search box is empty sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns sortAttributes(attributes) unfiltered. The attributes the change intends to hide therefore remain visible in the default Attributes view and only disappear after the user types a search query.

findings.title: Reports with neither age nor timestamp pass validation
findings.body: BrowserReportSerializer declares both age and timestamp as required=False, and validate_age/validate_timestamp only reject the case where the other field is present in initial_data. A report containing neither field is accepted even though the two supported Reporting API specs each require one of them, and a report with age=0 plus a timestamp also passes because the checks use truthiness (self.initial_data.get('age') / .get('timestamp')) rather than presence. Malformed reports are then counted in metrics as valid browser reports.

findings.title: Error events are interleaved using mismatched timestamp units
findings.body: gen_request_data compares error_events timestamps directly against replay segment event timestamps. Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, which stores timestamp as seconds since epoch, while rrweb/replay segment event timestamps are milliseconds since epoch. Every error timestamp (~1.7e9) is therefore always less than every segment timestamp (~1.7e12), so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb regardless of when they occurred, producing a chronologically wrong log sequence for the Seer summary. The new unit test masks this by using second-scale timestamps for the fake segment events.

findings.title: Analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...) runs unconditionally at the start of post(), before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check that returns 404 and before request-body validation that can return 400. Assemble events are therefore recorded for organizations without the feature and for malformed requests that never assemble anything, polluting the analytics used to measure adoption of this endpoint.

findings.title: AI summary shows 'Project not found' while the project is still loading
findings.body: The new guard `if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)` runs before the isPending check. useProjectFromId returns undefined while its project request is in flight, so on first render for a valid replay the tab immediately renders the 'Project not found. Unable to load AI summary.' error instead of a loading state; the error is incorrect and flashes (or sticks if the summary query's enabled state is tied to the same render cycle) for projects that do exist.
